overrideReason: All 3 automated attempts failed with 'gates failed: test'. Attempts 2-3 additionally show the implementer itself exiting 1 before doing any work ('You've hit your usage limit... try again at 1:55 PM' in attempt 3's raw stdout) - confirmed via .uf/runs/US-807-a{2,3}-*/implement/stdout.log - so all 3 attempts verified the same underlying diff from attempt 1, not 3 independent tries. Investigated the real cause directly rather than assuming a repeat of a known pattern. Found and fixed two genuine, distinct defects: (1) tests/test_assets.py's isinstance whitelist for run.indicators values (used by test_all_four_assets_produce_an_indicator_value_or_explicit_status) was never updated to include FredOk, SosoValueEtfFlowOk, or DefiLlamaStablecoinSupplyOk even though those types were already imported in the file - a real gap in the implementer's own diff, not a verifier artifact. Fixed by adding all three to both isinstance tuples in the file. (2) Running the story's own C5 integration test locally (tests/test_persist_board.py::test_live_scheduled_board_run_persists_registry_minus_sol_active_addresses) first failed with 11/84 live indicators erroring on 'FRED_API_KEY is not configured' plus SoSoValue failures - traced to a shell-session artifact (this repo's .env.local is not auto-loaded; exporting it fixed the local run) but this pointed at a real, separate, more serious production gap: .github/workflows/ingest.yml's env block was never updated to pass FRED_API_KEY or SOSOVALUE_API_KEY to the daily-tier CI job at all, even though the daily tier now depends on both (confirmed: the two most recent feature-branch CI runs, for the US-804 and US-805 commits, both already failed in production for this exact reason - gh run list shows both as 'completed failure'). Fixed by adding both secrets to ingest.yml's env block. A real live CI dispatch after that fix (run 36401042727) then failed with a THIRD distinct real defect: psycopg.errors.UndefinedColumn: column "reference_period" of relation "datapoints" does not exist - US-801's migration (20260927120000_add_datapoint_reference_period_and_published_at.sql) had been written, checksummed, and verified against a throwaway test schema, but never actually applied to the live production database's public schema. This is the exact same class of gap this project has hit before (PRD-003's G4, and US-507/US-510 in PRD-005, both documented in SESSION.md: 'tests run against TEST_DATABASE_URL, so they proved the migration was correct and never that it was applied'). ingest/migrate.py only supports --check, with no apply path, by design - migrations are applied to production by hand. This is a blast-radius action (database migration) per AGENTS.md, so I asked the owner for explicit authorization before running it; the owner approved. Applied the migration directly against the production DATABASE_URL (confirmed columns absent beforehand via a live schema query, confirmed present after), ran notify pgrst, 'reload schema', and confirmed board_read/datapoints_read views expose both new columns. Re-dispatched the real ingest workflow (run 36425805380, workflow_dispatch on feat/prd-008-macro-flows): completed successfully in 2m17s, exit 0. Also re-ran the local live C5 integration test with .env.local exported: passed, 84 rows persisted, failure rate 0/84 well under the 10% tolerance. Full local suite verified clean on current HEAD: npm --prefix web run typecheck clean, npm --prefix web test 53/53 passed, uv run mypy ingest --strict clean, uv run ruff check clean, uv run pytest -q -m "not integration" 339 passed.

results.note: tests/test_persist_board.py::test_persist_board_has_one_path_for_technical_derivatives_onchain_macro_and_flows passes. persist_board (ingest/pipeline.py:726) uses generic getattr(result, "source_field"/"reference_period"/"published_at", None) duck-typing across every Ok variant (Ok, FundingRateOk, ..., FredOk, SosoValueEtfFlowOk, DefiLlamaStablecoinSupplyOk, AlternativeMeFearGreedOk) - no macro-specific branch exists in the function.

tests/test_persist_board.py::test_full_run_writes_one_datapoint_row_per_computed_indicator and test_daily_tier_entry_point_persists_only_daily_board_rows_and_pings_once both pass, covering every registered FRED/SoSoValue/DefiLlama/alternative.me row alongside the existing technical/derivatives/on-chain rows in one run.

tests/test_persist_board.py::test_one_macro_flow_fetch_failure_persists_error_and_all_categories_continue passes: a forced macro/flows failure persists as Error while every other category's cells continue to persist normally.

tests/test_persist_board.py::test_daily_tier_entry_point_persists_only_daily_board_rows_and_pings_once passes: the heartbeat pings success exactly once per completed run regardless of individual cell status.

tests/test_persist_board.py::test_live_scheduled_board_run_persists_registry_minus_sol_active_addresses re-run fresh with real credentials and the applied production migration: PASSED. 84 rows persisted (matches the full daily-tier registry), 0/84 live-indicator failures, all four new categories (macro_*, spot_etf_net_flow, stablecoin_supply, fear_greed_index) present with correct counts (7/3/3/1).

Real GitHub Actions dispatch of .github/workflows/ingest.yml on feat/prd-008-macro-flows after both fixes (FRED_API_KEY/SOSOVALUE_API_KEY added to the workflow env, and the production migration applied): run https://github.com/haz18zayour/crypto-data-live-platform/actions/runs/36425805380 completed successfully in 2m17s, exit 0.

note: All 6 criteria independently verified. This story surfaced three distinct, genuinely undiscoverable-without-live-action defects layered on top of each other: a test whitelist gap (fixable from code alone), a CI workflow missing two required secrets in its env block (only visible from a real CI run against production, not from the offline workflow-text test), and a written-but-never-applied database migration (only visible from a real live/CI run against the actual public schema, exactly the class of gap this project's own SESSION.md already documents from PRD-003 and PRD-005). The database migration was applied to production only after asking the owner for explicit authorization, consistent with AGENTS.md's blast-radius policy for database migrations.
